commonMistakes: Failing to destarch a plant before a controlled investigation.
Using an everyday description without the defining scientific feature.
Pairing by a familiar word rather than the full scientific meaning.
Answering generally without covering every requested part or mark point.
detailedExplanation: Historical and leaf-starch experiments provide evidence for the requirements and products of photosynthesis.

Explain biological ideas as linked steps: name the structure or process, state what happens, and connect it to the effect on the cell, organism or ecosystem. Use precise scientific terms rather than everyday substitutes.
examTips: Give the purpose of each step as well as the method.
Link the controlled difference to the scientific conclusion.
Use the command word and number of marks to decide how many distinct points are required.
Use precise terminology and link cause to effect rather than listing disconnected facts.
For calculations, show the relationship, substitution, working and unit.
